paragraphs.sourceText: Listen to the following passage. Altogether the passage will be read to you four times. During the first reading, which will be done at normal speed, listen and try to understand the meaning. For the second and third readings, the passage, except the first sentence, will be read sentence by sentence, or phrase by phrase, with intervals of 15 seconds. The last reading will be read at normal speed again and during this time you should check your work. You will then be given ONE minute to check your work once more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 听下面这段话。这篇文章总共会读给你四遍。在第一次阅读时，将以正常速度完成，聆听并尝试理解其含义。第二、三读时，除第一句外，逐句或逐词朗读，间隔15秒。最后一次阅读将再次以正常速度阅读，在此期间您应该检查您的作业。然后您将有一分钟的时间再次检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Write on ANSWER SHEET ONE. The first sentence of the passage is already provided.
paragraphs.translationZh: 写在第一张答题纸上。该段落的第一句话已经提供。

paragraphs.sourceText: Gestures are movements made with body parts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 手势是用身体部位做出的动作。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear a talk. You will hear the talk ONCE ONLY. While listening, you may look at the task on ANSWER SHEET ONE and write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each gap. Make sure what you fill in is both grammatically and semantically acceptable. You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到一场演讲。您只会听到一次演讲。听力时，您可以查看第一张答题卡上的任务，并为每个空白写不超过三个单词。确保您填写的内容在语法和语义上都是可接受的。您可以使用空白纸做笔记。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览填补空白的任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now listen to the talk. When it is over, you will be given TWO minutes to check your work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在听一下演讲。结束后，您将有两分钟时间检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear two conversations. At the end of each conversation, five questions will be asked about what was said. Both the conversations and the questions will be spoken ONCE ONLY. After each question there will be a ten-second pause. During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C and D, and mark the best answer to each question on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到两个对话。每次对话结束时，都会针对谈话内容提出五个问题。对话和问题都只会说一次。每个问题后都会有十秒钟的停顿。暂停期间，您应该阅读 A、B、C、D 四个选项，并在第二张答题卡上标记每个问题的最佳答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the choices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览选项。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to the conversations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，听听对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 to 5 are based on Conversation One.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 1 至 5 基于对话一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 6 to 10 are based on Conversation Two.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 6 至 10 基于对话二。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are twenty sentences in this section. Beneath each sentence there are four options marked A, B, C and D. Choose
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节共有二十句话。每个句子下面有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择

paragraphs.sourceText: the one that best completes the sentence or answers the question. Mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最能完成句子或回答问题的人。在第二张答题卡上标记您的答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: 11. The smell that rose from the saucepan was so powerful that Mom shut the window lest anybody outside ______ it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 11. 平底锅里散发出的气味太浓烈了，妈妈关上了窗户，以免外面有人______。

paragraphs.sourceText: 12. George told the police officer that he was punched ______ by a masked man Sunday night at a restaurant.
paragraphs.translationZh: 12. 乔治告诉警察，他周日晚上在一家餐馆被一名蒙面男子殴打______。

paragraphs.sourceText: 13. The printer used the highest quality paper and ink and turned out far fewer volumes than he otherwise ______.
paragraphs.translationZh: 13. 打印机使用了最高质量的纸张和墨水，并且打印出的卷数比其他方式要少得多 ______。

paragraphs.sourceText: 14. The unemployment rate kept rising in that decade, ______ did economic growth accompanied by rampant commercialism and consumerism.
paragraphs.translationZh: 14. 那十年失业率不断上升，______经济增长伴随着商业主义和消费主义的猖獗。

paragraphs.sourceText: 15. In the coming years, there are about 10,000 square kilometers of the designated search area still ______ by sonar equipment towed from ships.
paragraphs.translationZh: 15. 未来几年，仍有约 10,000 平方公里的指定搜索区域______由船上拖曳的声纳设备覆盖。

paragraphs.sourceText: 16. Despite their high profile and increasing athletic ability, ______ might still lag behind men in participation, events, and medals awarded.
paragraphs.translationZh: 16. 尽管______知名度很高，运动能力不断增强，但他们在参与度、赛事和奖牌方面仍可能落后于男性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 17. Which of the following italicized phrases indicates CAUSE?
paragraphs.translationZh: 17. 以下哪个斜体短语表示原因？

paragraphs.sourceText: 18. “Perhaps you could pick up the book at my flat at some time that suited you?” The underlined verb forms are used to indicate ______.
paragraphs.translationZh: 18.“也许你可以在适合你的时间到我的公寓取这本书？”带下划线的动词形式用于表示______。

paragraphs.sourceText: 19. “My 60 application letters procured just one interview, which I declined.” The non-restrictive relative clause in the sentence is used to ______.
paragraphs.translationZh: 19.“我的 60 封求职信只获得了一次面试机会，但我拒绝了。”句子中的非限制性关系从句用于______。

paragraphs.sourceText: 20. In which of the following sentences does the preposition “beneath” carry a metaphorical sense?
paragraphs.translationZh: 20.下列哪个句子中介词“before”带有隐喻意义？

paragraphs.sourceText: 21. The ______ conclusion by scientists until recently had been that rising air temperatures were causing the Antarctic
paragraphs.translationZh: 21. 直到最近，科学家们得出的______结论是，气温上升导致了南极洲

paragraphs.sourceText: Peninsula to melt.
paragraphs.translationZh: 半岛融化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 22. Ecologists have been analyzing more than 500,000 plant ______ and finding 11,676 different tree types in the rainforest.
paragraphs.translationZh: 22. 生态学家分析了超过 500,000 种植物 ______，并在雨林中发现了 11,676 种不同的树木类型。

paragraphs.sourceText: 23. Unable to continue at her job and to pay rent, Vicky and her family were ______ from their home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 23. 由于无法继续工作和支付房租，Vicky 和她的家人被______ 驱逐出家。

paragraphs.sourceText: 24. The archaeological dig is almost without ______ the most revelatory of its kind, it has begun to transform our knowledge of life in the Bronze Age.
paragraphs.translationZh: 24. 考古发掘几乎没有______同类中最具启发性的，它已经开始改变我们对青铜时代生活的认识。

paragraphs.sourceText: 25. Both official and unofficial records indicate that the war ______ over 6 million people, resulting in the creation of the largest refugee population worldwide today.
paragraphs.translationZh: 25. 官方和非官方记录均表明，战争______导致超过600万人死亡，造成当今世界上最大的难民人口。

paragraphs.sourceText: 26. Few are spared from suffering in The Kite Runner, and the author ______ from offering a simplistic happy ending.
paragraphs.translationZh: 26. 在《追风筝的人》中，几乎没有人能幸免于苦难，而作者 ______ 也提供了一个简单化的幸福结局。

paragraphs.sourceText: 27. Through the story of two boys, this haunting and ______ tale demonstrates the importance of preserving our humanity at all costs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 27. 通过两个男孩的故事，这个令人难忘的 ______ 故事展示了不惜一切代价保护人性的重要性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 28. The editor of Merriam-Webster pointed out that there are many reasons to look up a word in the dictionary ______ than learning its meaning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 28. 《韦氏词典》的编辑指出，在字典中查找单词______比了解其含义有很多原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: 29. Ten soldiers were ambushed and ______ injured after the gunmen attacked the camp late at night.
paragraphs.translationZh: 29. 枪手深夜袭击营地后，十名士兵遭到伏击，______ 受伤。

paragraphs.sourceText: 30. Although Gutenburg developed his printing press with a limited use in mind, the cultural effects of mass printing have been ______.
paragraphs.translationZh: 30. 尽管古腾堡在开发印刷机时考虑到了有限的用途，但大规模印刷的文化影响却是______。

paragraphs.sourceText: Decide which of the words given in the box below would best complete the passage if inserted in the corresponding blank. The words can be used ONCE ONLY. Mark the letter for each word on ANSWER SHEET TWO.

Reality is always a mutually agreed-upon social construct, a more or less common consensus about what is out there and what it all means to most people. Our shared ideas of truth, beauty, morality, politics, and the (31) ______ we interpret the world and make decisions on how we act in it are determined by a complex process of education, (32) ______, acculturation, and assent that begins at birth. It is a cliché that human beings are out of touch with nature, and that more than a few of us are out of touch with reality. The fact is, (33) ______ when we are in touch, it’s not with some given natural world or some (34) ______ existing reality. Being in touch with nature means acting (35) ______ learned response to the natural world. As a matter of fact, responding with awe in the (36) ______ of natural beauty dates back only to the eighteenth century and became a major cultural event only in the nineteenth century. Before the late seventeenth century, people in Western Europe did not pay much attention to nature’s grandeur. A mountain range was something in the way. A complex shift in sociological and (37) ______ responses occurred in the early eighteenth century and can be traced in its development through travel literature and then in poetry, fiction, and philosophy. By the mid-eighteenth century, wild, mountainous landscapes became the site of grand, (38) ______ emotional response. The mountains had not, themselves, changed; cultural response had. The “Sublime”, the effect of (39) ______ transported before nature’s wildness and in front of representations of that wildness in painting and poetry, was born. With it came nineteenth-century romanticism and attitudes toward the natural world that (40) ______ remain with us. Reality is not an objective, geophysical phenomenon like a mountain. Reality is always something said or understood about the world.

In this section there are three passages followed by ten multiple choice questions. For each multiple choice question, there are four suggested answers marked A, B, C and D. Choose the one that you think is the best answer and mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节由三篇文章组成，后面是十个多项选择题。对于每个多项选择题，有四个建议答案，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择您认为最佳答案的一个，并将您的答案标记在答题表二上。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) We didn’t always live on Mango Street. Before that we lived on Loomis on the third floor, and before that we lived on Keeler. Before Keeler it was Paulina, and before that I can’t remember. But what I remember most is moving a lot. Each time it seemed there’d be one more of us. By the time we got to Mango Street we were six-Mama, Papa, Carlos, Kiki, my sister Nenny and me.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 我们并不总是住在芒果街。在此之前我们住在Loomis的三楼，再之前我们住在Keeler。在基勒之前是宝琳娜，之前我不记得了。但我记得最深的是感动了很多。每一次，我们似乎都会多一个人。当我们到达芒果街时，我们已经有六人了——妈妈、爸爸、卡洛斯、琪琪、妹妹妮妮和我。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) The house on Mango Street is ours, and we don’t have to pay rent to anybody, or share the yard with the people downstairs, or be careful not to make too much noise, and there isn’t a landlord banging on the ceiling with a broom. But even so, it’s not the house we’d thought we’d get.
paragraphs.translationZh: （2）芒果街的房子是我们的，我们不用向任何人交房租，也不用和楼下的人共用一个院子，也不用注意不要发出太大的噪音，也没有房东拿着扫帚敲打天花板。但即便如此，这也不是我们想要得到的房子。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) We had to leave the flat on Loomis quick. The water pipes broke and the landlord wouldn’t fix them because the house was too old. We had to leave fast. We were using the washroom next door and carrying water over in empty milk gallons. That’s why Mama and Papa looked for a house, and that’s why we moved into the house on Mango Street, far away, on the other side of town.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 我们必须尽快离开卢米斯的公寓。水管坏了，房东不肯修，因为房子太旧了。我们不得不快速离开。我们正在使用隔壁的洗手间，并用空牛奶加仑运水。这就是妈妈和爸爸找房子的原因，这就是为什么我们搬进了芒果街的房子，很远，在城镇的另一边。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) They always told us that one day we would move into a house, a real house that would be ours for always so we wouldn’t have to move each year. And our house would have running water and pipes that worked. And inside it would have real stairs, not hallway stairs, but stairs inside like the houses on TV. And we’d have a basement and at least three washrooms so when we took a bath we wouldn’t have to tell everybody. Our house would be white with trees around it, a great big yard and grass growing without a fence. This was the house Papa talked about when he held a lottery ticket and this was the house Mama dreamed up in the stories she told us before we went to bed.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 他们总是告诉我们，有一天我们会搬进一所房子，一栋永远属于我们的真正的房子，这样我们就不用每年搬家了。我们的房子会有自来水和可用的管道。里面会有真正的楼梯，不是走廊楼梯，而是像电视里的房子一样的内部楼梯。我们有一个地下室和至少三个洗手间，这样我们洗澡时就不必告诉所有人。我们的房子是白色的，周围有树，有一个很大的院子，没有栅栏的草丛。这是爸爸拿着彩票时谈论的房子，这是妈妈在我们睡觉前给我们讲的故事中梦想的房子。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) But the house on Mango Street is not the way they told it at all. It’s small and red with tight steps in front and windows so small you’d think they were holding their breath. Bricks are crumbling in places, and the front door is so swollen you have to push hard to get in. There is no front yard, only four little elms the city planted by the curb. Our back is a small garage for the car we don’t own yet and a small yard that looks smaller between the two buildings on either side. There are stairs in our house, but they’re ordinary hallway stairs, and the house has only one washroom. Everybody has to share a bedroom-Mama and Papa, Carlos and Kiki, me and Nenny.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 但芒果街的房子根本不是他们说的那样。它又小又红，前面有狭窄的台阶，窗户小得让人以为他们屏住了呼吸。有些地方的砖块都在崩塌，前门肿得需要用力推才能进去。没有前院，只有四棵城里种在路边的小榆树。我们的后面是一个小车库，用来存放我们还没有拥有的汽车，还有一个小院子，在两边的两栋建筑之间看起来更小。我们家有楼梯，但都是普通的走廊楼梯，房子里只有一间洗手间。每个人都必须共用一间卧室——妈妈和爸爸、卡洛斯和琪琪、我和妮妮。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) Once when we were living on Loomis, a nun from my school passed by and saw me playing out front. The laundromat downstairs had been boarded up because it had been robbed two days before and the owner had painted on the wood YES WE’RE OPEN so as not to lose business.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 有一次，当我们住在卢米斯时，我们学校的一位修女路过，看到我在前面玩耍。楼下的自助洗衣店已经用木板封起来，因为两天前被抢劫了，店主在木头上画了“是的，我们正在营业”，以免失去生意。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Where do you live? She asked.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 你住在哪里？她问道。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) There, I said pointing up to the third floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 在那里，我指着三楼说道。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) You live there?
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 你住那儿？

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) There. I had to look to where she pointed-the third floor, the paint peeling, wooden bars Papa had nailed on the windows so we wouldn’t fall out. You live there? The way she said it made me feel like nothing. There. I lived there. I nodded.
paragraphs.translationZh: （10）那里。我不得不朝她指的地方看——三楼，油漆剥落，爸爸在窗户上钉了木条，这样我们就不会掉下来。你住那儿？她说这话的方式让我感觉自己什么都不是。那里。我住在那里。我点点头。

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) I knew then I had to have a house. A real house. One I could point to. But this isn’t it. The house on Mango Street isn’t it. For the time being, Mama says. Temporary, says Papa. But I know how those things go.
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) 那时我就知道我必须有一所房子。一座真正的房子。我可以指出的一个。但事实并非如此。芒果街上的那栋房子不是。妈妈说，暂时吧。爸爸说，是暂时的。但我知道事情是如何进行的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. The size of the family ______ each time they moved house.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 每次搬家时，______ 的家庭规模。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Which of the following does NOT fit the description of the family’s dream house (Para.4)?
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 以下哪项不符合该家庭梦想之家的描述（第 4 段）？

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The narrator’s dream house and the house on Mango Street are compared in the following details EXCEPT ______.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 除了______之外，叙述者的梦想之家和芒果街的房子在以下细节上进行了比较。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Thanksgiving may be an official day of gratitude in the U.S., but research suggests that if you make time for “thank you” every day, you might enjoy life more.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 感恩节在美国可能是一个正式的感恩节，但研究表明，如果你每天抽出时间说“谢谢”，你可能会更享受生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Many people may think of gratitude as a “passive” gesture-you wait for something good, then feel grateful, said David DeSteno, a professor of psychology at Northeastern University. DeSteno studies the effects that thankfulness can have on people’s behavior.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 东北大学心理学教授戴维·德斯特诺 (David DeSteno) 表示，许多人可能认为感恩是一种“被动”的姿态——你等待美好的事物，然后感到感激。德斯特诺研究感恩对人们行为的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) But a growing body of research is suggesting the opposite is true, according to DeSteno. By choosing to feel gratitude, people can make positive changes in their lives. “Gratitude isn’t passive reflection. It’s active,” DeSteno said. “And it’s not about the past. It’s there to help direct our behavior in the future.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 但德斯特诺表示，越来越多的研究表明事实恰恰相反。通过选择感恩，人们可以在生活中做出积极的改变。 “感恩不是被动的反思。它是主动的，”德斯特诺说。 “这与过去无关。它的存在是为了帮助指导我们未来的行为。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) In experiments where he and his colleagues set people up to feel grateful, they found that thankfulness appeared to spur participants to act in more cooperative, less selfish ways. In one study, for example, people came to the lab to complete a computer task. At some point, certain participants’ computers were rigged to “crash”. Luckily, a kind stranger who had just completed the same task (and was actually part of the research team) offered help and got the computer running again. Afterward, all of the study participants played a standard economic game where people have the opportunity to either act strictly in their own self-interest or in a more cooperative way.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 在他和他的同事让人们感到感恩的实验中，他们发现感恩似乎会刺激参与者以更加合作、更少自私的方式行事。例如，在一项研究中，人们来到实验室是为了完成一项计算机任务。在某些时候，某些参与者的计算机被操纵“崩溃”。幸运的是，一位刚刚完成相同任务的好心陌生人（实际上是研究团队的一员）提供了帮助，并使计算机重新运行起来。之后，所有研究参与者都玩了一个标准的经济游戏，人们有机会严格按照自己的利益行事，或者以更合作的方式行事。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) In general, DeSteno’s team found, the study participants who had gotten help from a stranger during that first test were more likely to be cooperative during the next test. (A survey all of the participants took confirmed that those who’d received help were, in fact, feeling more grateful than their counterparts who’d had smooth sailing.) That’s one of a number of studies, DeSteno said, that suggest that gratitude helps guide behavior. It can encourage you to get more exercises, or to be more helpful to others (and not just that person you feel you “owe”).
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) DeSteno 的团队发现，总的来说，在第一次测试中得到陌生人帮助的研究参与者在下一次测试中更有可能合作。 （对所有参与者进行的一项调查证实，那些获得帮助的人实际上比那些一帆风顺的同行感到更加感激。）德斯特诺说，这是众多研究之一，这些研究表明感恩有助于指导行为。它可以鼓励您进行更多锻炼，或者为他人（而不仅仅是您认为“欠”的人）提供更多帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) Some research has also found links between gratitude and better health, such as lower blood pressure and just feeling physically better. However, it’s not clear whether gratitude directly affects physical well-being.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 一些研究还发现感恩与更好的健康之间存在联系，例如降低血压和感觉身体更好。然而，尚不清楚感恩是否会直接影响身体健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) At the University of California, Professor Naomi Eisenberger and her colleagues hope to zero in a bit more on the effects of gratitude. For six weeks, some study participants will spend time writing about things for which they are grateful. The rest will write about positive subjects, but won’t focus on gratitude.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 加州大学的内奥米·艾森伯格教授和她的同事希望将感恩的影响归零。在六周的时间里，一些研究参与者会花时间写下他们感激的事情。其余的会写积极的主题，但不会关注感恩。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) According to Eisenberger, gratitude, based on studies like DeSteno’s, seems to enhance people’s ability to care for others. And in animals, Eisenberger noted, caregiving is linked to lesser reactivity in the face of a threat-mothers may feel less scared for themselves when a predator comes, and protect their babies instead.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 艾森伯格认为，基于德斯特诺等研究，感恩似乎可以增强人们关心他人的能力。艾森伯格指出，在动物中，照顾与面对威胁时的反应较小有关——当掠食者到来时，母亲可能不会那么害怕，而是会保护自己的婴儿。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) Whatever the biological effects, plenty of research suggests that gratitude can change how you feel-even about those people who’ve been in your life for years, according to Sara Algoe, an assistant professor of psychology at the University of North Carolina.
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 北卡罗来纳大学心理学助理教授萨拉·阿尔戈 (Sara Algoe) 表示，无论生物效应如何，大量研究表明，感恩可以改变你的感受，甚至改变你生活中多年的人的感受。

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) Her research has focused on the effects of gratitude in romantic relationships. In one study of 77 couples who’d been together for an average of four years, Algoe’s team had each partner think of something the other had done for them recently-no matter how small-and then thank him or her. Before that task, the couples completed a survey on their satisfaction with their relationship. Then they did it again six months later.
paragraphs.translationZh: (10) 她的研究重点是感恩对浪漫关系的影响。在一项对 77 对平均在一起四年的夫妇进行的研究中，阿尔戈的团队让每一对伴侣想想对方最近为他们做了一些事情——无论多小——然后感谢他或她。在这项任务之前，夫妻俩完成了一项关于他们的关系满意度的调查。六个月后他们又这样做了。

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) In general, the study saw a shift in people who felt their partner really meant that “thank you”- thinking, for example, that “my partner saw the ‘real’ me.” Those men and women typically felt more satisfied with their relationship six months later. The findings, according to Algoe, highlight the importance of saying “thank you” even for those mundane things, from those people you see every day.
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) 总的来说，这项研究发现人们发生了转变，他们认为自己的伴侣真的是在说“谢谢”——例如，认为“我的伴侣看到了‘真实’的我”。这些男人和女人通常在六个月后对他们的关系感到更加满意。阿尔戈表示，研究结果强调了即使是对那些平凡的事情，对那些你每天见到的人说“谢谢”的重要性。

paragraphs.sourceText: (12) “Expressing gratitude well is a potent part of relationship satisfaction,” Algoe said. “Sometimes we feel grateful, but we don’t say it. This research suggests it’s important to say it. And if someone offers you help, try accepting it instead of shunning it. See it as a gift.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (12)“良好地表达感激之情是关系满意度的一个重要组成部分，”阿尔戈说。 “有时我们会感到感激，但我们不会说出来。这项研究表明说出来很重要。如果有人向你提供帮助，请尝试接受而不是回避。将其视为一份礼物。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) As words fall in and out of fashion, new ones enter the language. But some, such as autonaut, chassimover and pupamotor failed to reach the assembly line.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 随着单词的流行和过时，新的单词进入语言。但有些产品，如自动驾驶仪、底盘车和蛹马达未能到达装配线。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) English is a marvelous mashup of words. A few Celtic place names. A stock of Old English words (day and night, black and white, food and drink). More than twice as many words adopted from Norman French (marriage, parliament). Sometimes competing words from both: motherhood (Old English) and maternity (Norman French). Words of Greek derivation, like octopus. Words of Latin derivation, such as campus and ultimatum. Words from all over the place: Welsh (corgi), Irish (brogues), Arabic (algebra), German (hamster), Chinese (typhoon), Japanese (tycoon), American Indian (tobacco), and many more.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 英语是单词的奇妙混搭。一些凯尔特地名。一组古英语单词（白天和黑夜、黑色和白色、食物和饮料）。诺曼法语中采用的单词（婚姻、议会）的数量是其两倍多。有时，两者的词相互竞争：motherhood（古英语）和maternity（诺曼法语）。希腊语衍生词，如章鱼。拉丁语衍生词，例如 Campus 和 ultimatum。来自世界各地的单词：威尔士语（柯基犬）、爱尔兰语（布洛克鞋）、阿拉伯语（代数）、德语（仓鼠）、汉语（台风）、日语（大亨）、美洲印第安语（烟草）等等。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) Wherever they come from, words fall in and out of fashion. Within living memory some words have changed meanings completely, while bad and wicked changed, then changed back. Yesterday’s slang is respectable today. In the 1950s and 60s, words that angered people who write to newspapers included job (the writer thought it vulgar, and preferred employment), and breakdown (“horrible jargon”). The Manchester Guardian stylebook of 1950 banned such “slang” phrases as bank on, face up to, give away, sack (for “dismiss”) and many others.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 无论词语来自何处，它们都会时时流行，时而过时。在人们的记忆中，有些词的含义已经完全改变，而“坏”和“邪恶”则改变了，然后又变回来。昨天的俚语今天仍然受人尊敬。在20世纪50年代和60年代，激怒写报纸的人的词语包括“工作”（作者认为它粗俗，更喜欢就业）和“崩溃”（“可怕的行话”）。 1950 年的《曼彻斯特卫报》风格手册禁止使用诸如 Bank on、face up to、giveaway、sack（意为“解雇”）等“俚语”短语。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) The expression “foregone conclusion” once meant an experience previously undergone, rather than making a decision without listening to the arguments. Many words we use today have a different meaning from 20,never mind 50,100 or 200 years ago. The word “nice”once meant silly (silly meant happy or blessed),then subtle, then pleasant. You could be sad with food and drink-it meant full to the brim, and was related to satisfied and saturated. It then came to mean solid, so a reliable person could be called sad; in time, solid, heavy and dull came to mean sad in one of our modern uses. In recent years it subtly acquired an additional meaning, as in “how sad is that?”
paragraphs.translationZh: （4）“预料之中的结论”一词曾经是指以前经历过的经历，而不是不听论证就做出决定。我们今天使用的许多单词的含义与 20 年前不同，更不用说 50,100 年前或 200 年前了。 “nice”这个词曾经意味着愚蠢（愚蠢意味着快乐或幸福），然后是微妙的，然后是愉快的。你可能会对食物和饮料感到悲伤——它意味着饱足，与满足和饱和有关。后来它的意思是“坚固”，所以可靠的人可以被称为悲伤的人。随着时间的推移，“坚实”、“沉重”和“沉闷”在我们现代的用法之一中逐渐意味着悲伤。近年来，它巧妙地获得了额外的含义，例如“那有多悲伤？”

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) About 1,700 words are first recorded in Shakespeare (which does not necessarily mean he invented them), including barefaced, fancy-free, laughable and submerged. Milton is credited with the expression “all ears”. Jung invented the word synchronicity as well as ambivalent, extrovert and introvert, while Freud came up with the word psychoanalysis, which is derived from the Greek for butterfly, psyche, who was also the Greek goddess of the soul.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 莎士比亚首次记录了大约 1,700 个单词（这并不一定意味着他发明了这些单词），包括“赤裸裸”、“无幻想”、“可笑”和“淹没”等。弥尔顿因“全神贯注”一词而闻名。荣格发明了“共时性”以及“矛盾性”、“外向性”和“内向性”这个词，而弗洛伊德则提出了“精神分析”这个词，该词源自希腊语，意为“蝴蝶”，“心灵”，也是希腊灵魂女神。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) There is another continual source of new words. The man who developed Bluetooth in 1996 was reading a historical novel about Harald Bluetooth, a 10th-century King of Denmark, at the time and appropriated his name. Spam, in the sense of unwanted emails, was named after the 1970 Monty Python cafe sketch in which Spam, in the sense of unwanted canned meat, was compulsory in every dish. Sometimes new words catch on, sometimes they don’t, but you can always bet that someone, somewhere will object to them. I recall readers complaining about the Guardian’s use of the new word blog (an abbreviation of another new word, weblog) but within a very short time it had become established. In the early 1960s, the Automobile Association sought suggestions from the public for a new word to describe drivers: submissions included autocarist, autonaut, chassimover, motorman, wheelist, and the bizarre acronym pupamotor (“person using power-assisted means of travelling on roads”). The idea was dropped. Whoever came up with laser (“light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation”) in 1960 was more successful.
paragraphs.translationZh: （6）新词还有另一个源源不断的来源。 1996 年开发蓝牙的人当时正在阅读一本关于 10 世纪丹麦国王哈拉尔·蓝牙 (Harald Bluetooth) 的历史小说，并盗用了他的名字。垃圾邮件（Spam）是指不需要的电子邮件，它是以 1970 年 Monty Python 咖啡馆的草图命名的，其中垃圾邮件（Spam）指的是不需要的罐头肉，是每道菜中必不可少的。有时新词会流行，有时不会，但你总可以打赌，某个地方的某人会反对它们。我记得读者抱怨《卫报》使用了新词“博客”（另一个新词“网络博客”的缩写），但在很短的时间内它就被确立了。 20 世纪 60 年代初，汽车协会向公众征求建议，寻找一个新词来描述驾驶员：提交的材料包括 autocarist、autonaut、chassimover、motorman、wheelist 以及奇怪的缩写词 pupamotor（“在道路上使用动力辅助方式行驶的人”）。这个想法被放弃了。 1960 年提出激光（“受激辐射光放大”）的人更为成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) The writer A. P. Herbert devised a scoring system for new words, which would be given marks out of 10 on each of four criteria: is it readily understood, is it to be admired, is it sound etymologically, and is it actually required? The pass mark was 50%and television, for example, just scraped through (scoring respectively 10, 0, 0, and 10). One of my favorite recent words is bouncebackability, a neat alternative to “the ability to bounce back” attributed to the former football manager Iain Dowie. I fear it would fail the test.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7)作家A.P.赫伯特设计了一个新词评分系统，根据四个标准每一项打分，满分10分：它是否容易理解，是否值得欣赏，它在词源上是否合理，是否确实需要？及格分数为 50%，而以电视为例，勉强及格（分别为 10、0、0 和 10）。我最近最喜欢的词之一是反弹能力，这是前足球经理伊恩·道伊所说的“反弹能力”的一个巧妙替代。我担心它会考试不及格。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now the trend towards banning plastic shopping bags comes in the wake of new findings regarding the extent and harm of plastic in our environment. Since plastic isn’t biodegradable, it ends up either in landfills or as litter on the landscape and in waterways and the ocean. Plastic can take hundreds of years to decompose and release toxins into the soil and water in the process.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，随着有关塑料在我们环境中的范围和危害的新发现，禁止使用塑料购物袋的趋势随之而来。由于塑料不可生物降解，因此它最终要么进入垃圾填埋场，要么作为景观、水道和海洋中的垃圾。塑料可能需要数百年的时间才能分解，并在此过程中将毒素释放到土壤和水中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Littered plastic is also a huge problem for the health of wildlife, as many animals ingest it thinking it is food and can have problems thereafter breathing and digesting. The non-profit Worldwatch Institute reports that at least 267 species of marine wildlife are known to have suffered from entanglement or ingestion of marine debris, most of which is composed of plastic. A recent study on the impact of litter on North Sea wildlife has found that some 90 percent of the birds examined had plastic in their stomachs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 乱扔的塑料对野生动物的健康也是一个巨大的问题，因为许多动物误认为它是食物而摄入塑料，之后可能会出现呼吸和消化问题。非盈利组织世界观察研究所报告称，已知至少有 267 种海洋野生动物因缠绕或吞食海洋垃圾而遭受损失，其中大部分是由塑料制成的。最近一项关于垃圾对北海野生动物影响的研究发现，约 90% 的受检鸟类胃里都有塑料。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another reason for banning plastic bags is their burden on fossil fuel. Plastic is not only made from petroleum: producing it typically requires a lot of fossil-fuel-derived energy. The fact that the use of milions, or even billions of plastic grocery bags each year means we are drilling for or are importing millions of barrels worth of oil and natural gas for a convenient way to carry home a few groceries
paragraphs.translationZh: 禁止塑料袋的另一个原因是它们对化石燃料的负担。塑料不仅由石油制成：生产塑料通常需要大量化石燃料能源。事实上，每年使用数百万甚至数十亿个塑料购物袋，这意味着我们正在钻探或进口价值数百万桶的石油和天然气，以便方便地将一些杂货带回家

paragraphs.sourceText: Environmental groups have continued to push for more plastic bag bans. They argue that using fossil fuel to make something so short-lived, which can blow away at the slightest breeze and pollutes indefinitely, is illogical, particularly when there is a ready alternative: the reusable bag.
paragraphs.translationZh: 环保组织继续推动更多塑料袋禁令。他们认为，使用化石燃料来制造寿命如此短暂的东西，微风吹过，就会无限期地污染，这是不合逻辑的，特别是当有现成的替代品：可重复使用的袋子时。

Why has the McDonald’s model proven so irresistible? Eating fast food at McDonald’s has certainly become a “sign” that, among other things, one is in tune with the contemporary lifestyle. There’s also a kind of magic or (31) ______ associated with such food and their settings. However, what will be focused on here are the four alluring dimensions that lie at the (32) ______ of the success of this model. In (33) ______, McDonald’s has succeeded because it offers consumers, workers, and managers efficiency, calculability, predictability and control.

One important element of McDonald’s success is efficiency, or the optimum (34) ______ for getting from one point to another. For consumers, McDonald’s offers the best available way to get from being hungry to being full. In a society where both parents are likely to work or where a single parent is (35) ______ to raise children on her own, efficiently satisfying hunger is very attractive.

Calculability is an emphasis on the quantitative aspects of products sold (portion size, cost) and services offered (the time it takes to get the product). In McDonaldized systems, quantity has become equivalent to quality; a lot of something, or the quick (36) ______ of it, means it must be good.

McDonald’s also offers predictability, the (37) ______ that products and services will be the same over time and in all locales. The Egg McMuffin in New York will be (38) ______ to those in Chicago and Los Angeles. Also, those eaten next week or next year will be the same as those eaten today.

The fourth element in McDonald’s success, control, is (39) ______ over people who enter the world of McDonald’s. Lines, limited menus, (40) ______ options all lead diners to do what management wishes them to do — eat quickly and leave.
